title: The paddock that grew
summary: Keith's first book, about the origins and history of the Melbourne Cricket Ground, tracing its transformation from a swampy paddock beside the Yarra into Australia's premier sporting arena.

title: Supporting a column
summary: Reflects on the trials of taking on a daily column in the Sun News-Pictorial, a behind-the-scenes account of Australian newspaper life in the 1950s and 60s.

title: Wowsers
summary: Documents the prudery of an early Australia aiming to shed its image as a place of convicts and rough behaviour.

title: The Australian Uppercrust Book
summary: A collection of essays dissecting snobbery across Australian society; Keith contributed the chapter on 'Snobbery in Business'.

title: Knockers
summary: Examines the Australian habit of denigrating success and cutting down tall poppies.

title: Sports
summary: Looks at the Australian obsession with sport and sporting heroes, from suburban football fields to the country's biggest sporting institutions.

title: The store on the hill
summary: The story of Georges, the luxury Collins Street department store famed for its hushed, exclusive service.

title: Moomba, the first 25 years
summary: A silver-jubilee history of Melbourne's Moomba festival, published to mark 25 years of the city's biggest annual community celebration.

title: It's all up hill
summary: An illustrated account of travels and cycling around the United States, written with cartoonist Jeff Hook during Dunstan's posting as the Herald's US correspondent.

title: Ratbags
summary: Profiles Australia's great eccentrics, from Bea Miles to Percy Grainger.

title: Saint Ned
summary: A light-hearted look at the life of bushranger Ned Kelly and the growth of the Kelly legend into an industry of its own.

title: A cricket dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of cricket terms and jargon, illustrated by cartoonist Jeff Hook.

title: Footy, an Aussie rules dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of Australian Rules football terms and jargon, illustrated by Jeff Hook.

title: Tennis: a tennis dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of tennis terms and jargon, illustrated by Jeff Hook.

title: Above Australia: a salute to our cities
summary: A large-format collection of aerial photography of Australia's capital cities, with text contributions from Dunstan and fellow journalists.

title: Health and fitness: the dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of health, fitness and exercise jargon, illustrated by Jeff Hook.

title: Racing: the horse-racing dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of horse-racing terms and jargon, illustrated by Jeff Hook.

title: Wine, the wine dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of wine and wine-tasting jargon, illustrated by Jeff Hook.

title: Bowls, the lawn bowls dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of lawn bowls terms and jargon, illustrated by Jeff Hook.

title: Gurney & Bluey & Curley
summary: A retrospective of cartoonist Alex Gurney's work, especially his comic strip Bluey and Curley, compiled by Gurney's son John Gurney with Dunstan.

title: Hook, line and sinker: the dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of fishing terms and jargon, illustrated by Jeff Hook, whose surname supplied the pun in the title.

title: Skiing, the skiing dictionary
summary: A comic glossary of skiing terms and jargon, illustrated by Jeff Hook.

title: The amber nectar
summary: A history of beer and brewing in Australia, and the drink's central place in Australian social life.

title: Bundy: a centenary history
summary: A company history of Bundaberg Rum, commissioned to mark the distillery's 1988 centenary.

title: A Day in the Life of Australia
summary: An historical account of Australia for each day of the year, commissioned by The Age for the 1988 bicentennial.

title: The perfect cup: the story of coffee
summary: A history of coffee, its cultivation and trade, and its rise in Australian café culture.

title: No brains at all
summary: Keith's first book of memoirs, covering his career in writing, reflections on Melbourne, working abroad and his family life.

title: No brains on Tuesday
summary: A compilation of the best of Keith Dunstan's newspaper columns, gathering decades of his wit and observations on Australian life.

title: Flag, the first 30 years
summary: Commissioned by the Flag International hotel and motel group to mark its 30th anniversary, tracing the growth of the Australasian hospitality industry.

title: My life with the demon
summary: Recounts Keith's experiences with, around and under the influence of the Demon Drink, from boozy newsroom culture to Melbourne's six o'clock swill.

title: Just Jeans: The Story
summary: A corporate history of Just Jeans, commissioned to mark the Melbourne denim retailer's twenty-fifth anniversary.

title: The confessions of a bicycle nut
summary: Recounts a lifelong passion for cycling, from founding the Bicycle Institute of Victoria to touring by bicycle across the United States and through China.

title: Not a bad drop: Brown Brothers
summary: A history of Brown Brothers, the Milawa winemaking family, tracing four generations of the business.

title: The people's ground: the MCG
summary: A revised and updated edition of Dunstan's first book, retracing the Melbourne Cricket Ground's history for a new generation.

title: Informed sources: a history of the Melbourne Press Club 1971-2001
summary: A history of the Melbourne Press Club, of which Dunstan was president, tracing the club from its 1971 founding through its first thirty years.

title: 1853-2003, Victoria Police Australia
summary: A pictorial history marking 150 years of Victoria Police, with an introduction by Dunstan.

title: Batman in the Bulletin: The Melbourne I Remember
summary: A collection of Keith's columns written under the pseudonym 'Batman' for the Bulletin magazine, a wry record of Melbourne life and characters.

title: Collins: the story of Australia's premier street
summary: A richly illustrated history of Collins Street, Melbourne's premier boulevard, with contributions from Keith Dunstan.

title: Moonee Ponds to Broadway
summary: A study of Keith's friend and fellow Melburnian Barry Humphries, tracing his journey from suburban Melbourne to international stardom as Dame Edna Everage.

title: Two old geezers tell you about bridge, the A-Z
summary: A conversational, plain-English guide to the card game bridge, co-written with cartoonist Jeff Hook.

title: Kiwi: The Australian brand that brought a shine to the world
summary: Traces the story of the Ramsay family, who founded the Kiwi shoe polish brand in Melbourne in 1906 and built it into a global business.
